I am deeply disappointed, bitter, and hurt by the way my beloved cat's health was handled by Dr. Giuseppe.
A year ago, she was diagnosed with kidney failure, and since then I have monitored her consistently and attentively, taking her for regular checkups. Despite this, in recent months her condition has progressively worsened: she began suffering from frequent constipation, her abdomen was visibly swollen, and I, concerned, turned to Dr. Giuseppe again.
The answer? Every time the cat couldn't defecate, I was told to take her for an enema. The doctor dismissed the problem as back pain, without ever delving deeper. But I could see with my own eyes that something was wrong. Until, one day, my cat began to walk with difficulty: she struggled to move, she seemed disoriented.
I took her back to him immediately. The exam was hasty, and the verdict: "It's neurological." Without any tests, without any doubts, he sends us home with a prescription for gabapentin. The drug makes the situation worse: my cat appears dazed, lethargic, almost absent. We stop it immediately. But something has snapped. From that moment on, she has never been the same again.
When she has completely stopped walking, driven by desperation, I insist that we finally perform an abdominal ultrasound. Only then does a very serious situation emerge: thickened intestinal walls, the suspicion of a widespread tumor. The doctor appears surprised. Surprised. As if he had never truly examined her thoroughly, as if all those weeks of symptoms hadn't been enough to understand that there was something much, much more serious.
In a panic, I rush to another veterinarian, an oncology specialist. She paints a heartbreaking picture: a widespread tumor mass, possible intestinal perforation. She explains that, had it been discovered a month earlier, a histological exam could have been performed, a precise diagnosis of lymphoma could have been made, and treatment could have been started. Instead, time had been wasted.
We tried everything: hospitalization, intensive care. But it was too late. After a few days, my cat was gone. Without even having had a real chance.
Dr. Giuseppe's superficiality and superficiality condemned my cat. She wasn't given the opportunity to truly fight the disease that afflicted her.
And as if all this weren't enough, every uncertainty, every symptom, was trivialized with the following phrase: "Well, she's an old cat...". But he himself, years ago, estimated her age: in 2014, he told us she was about two years old. Today he claims she was seventeen.
Now all I'm left with is the pain. The memory of the last months of her life, marked by suffering and a disease that was never truly cured. But above all, the bitter knowledge that all this could perhaps have been avoided weighs heavily!
